AGENDA
  GLENDALE WATER & POWER COMMISSION
  VIA TELECONFERENCE ONLY
 Welcome to the meeting of the Glendale Water & Power Commission. Meetings are broadcast live
 on cable channel 6 (GTV6) and rebroadcast throughout the week. Call (818) 548-4013 for program
 schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City Clerk’s Office. Meetings
 are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at
 https://www.glendaleca.gov/government/public-meeting-portal. If you have any question about
 matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the Glendale Water & Power
 Administration Office at (818) 548-2107 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE COUNCIL CHAMBER.
 In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
 language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
 are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
 requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents related
 to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and
 are public records, will be available for review in the Glendale Water & Power Administration Office,
 141 N. Glendale Ave., Suite 450, Glendale, CA 91206.
 Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
 wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
 Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
 the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
 required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.
  FEBRUARY 1, 2021 AT 4:00 PM

Due to the evolving situation with the COVID-19 novel coronavirus and health recommendations from
the LA County Health Department, the Glendale Water & Power Commission meeting will be
available to the public electronically.

Due to social distancing requirements, the public will not be able to attend the meeting. The public is
encouraged to watch and participate from the safety of their homes to practice social distancing.

The meeting can be viewed:
On local cable: Charter Cable Channel 6 and AT&T U-verse Channel 99.
Streaming Online: https://www.glendaleca.gov/government/public-meeting-portal

For public comments and questions during the meeting call (818) 937-8100.

during the Glendale Water & Power Commission meeting.

1.  ROLL CALL – 4:00 PM
2.  CONSENT ITEMS – (INCLUDING MINUTES)
  The following are routine and may be acted upon by one motion. Any member of the
  Commission or the audience requesting separate consideration may do so by making such
  request before motion is proposed.
  a. Approval of the October 5, 2020 Meeting Minutes
  b. Approval of the November 2, 2020 Meeting Minutes
3.  GWP COMMISSION/STAFF COMMENTS
4.  ACTIONS
  a. GWP Commission Election (President and Secretary)
5.  REPORTS - INFORMATION
  a. Renewable Portfolio Standard, Clean Energy, and Power Content Label
  b. 4kv to 12 kv Conversation Program Update
  c. Grayson Energy Center CEQA Update
6.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS (5) Minutes
  Discussion is limited to items NOT part of this agenda. Each speaker is allowed five (5)
  minutes – Commission may question or respond to the speaker, but there will be no debate or

  a. Agenda Forecast

MINUTES
  GLENDALE WATER & POWER COMMISSION

  VIA TELECONFERENCE

  Monday, February 01, 2021, 4:00 PM

Due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, social distancing requirements, and health recommendations
from LA County Public Health Department, this meeting was conducted remotely. All GWP Commission
members and staff utilized video conferencing in order to virtually participate in the meeting.

1. ROLL CALL
  The meeting was called to order at 4:00 p.m.

  Present: President Kedikian, Commissioners Flanigan, Jazmadarian, Lall, and Peterson.

  President Kedikian and Commissioners Flanigan and Lall welcomed new GWP Commissioner
  Joel Peterson, who City Council member Ardashes Kassakhian appointed. Commissioner
  Peterson introduced himself and expressed that he looks forward to serving on the Commission.

2. CONSENT ITEMS
  a. Approval of the October 5, 2020 Meeting Minutes
  Minutes were approved by the Commission.

  b. Approval of the November 2, 2020 Meeting Minutes
  Commissioner Flanigan noted a grammatical error (missing sentence on Item 3.a, end of the
  second paragraph); the minutes were approved by the Commission as amended.

3. GWP COMMISSION/ STAFF COMMENTS
  Mark Young, Interim General Manager – GWP for February, explained that the Assistant General
  Managers and Chief Assistant General Managers for GWP would each take a turn performing
  the duties of Interim General Manager for GWP for a month until the position is filled. Mr. Young
  also welcomed new Commissioner Joel Peterson and commended outgoing GWP
  Commissioner Hrand Avanessian for his hard work during his term. Commissioner President
  Kedikian and Commissioner Lall also thanked former Commissioner Avanessian. Additionally,
  Commissioner Lall thanked Steve Zurn, former General Manager of GWP, for his many years of
  service to the City and hoped to wish him well at a future date once the pandemic subsides.

4. ACTION ITEMS
  a. GWP Commission Election (President and Secretary)
  Christine Godinez, Principal Assistant City Attorney, opened the nominations for the
  President and Secretary positions. A vote was held for each office. Commissioner Lall
  nominated Commissioner Jazmadarian for the position of Secretary, and President Kedikian
  nominated Commissioner Flanigan for GWP Commission President. Commissioner
  Jazmadarian was unanimously nominated for Secretary, and Commissioner Flanigan was
  unanimously appointed as President of the Commission. President Flanigan assumed the
  role of President for the remainder of the meeting.

  1
 5. REPORTS – INFORMATION
  a. Renewable Portfolio Standard and Power Content Label/Disclosure Report
  Mr. Young introduced Howard Wong, GWP Energy Risk Manager, to present the Renewable
  Portfolio Standard and Clean Energy Overview. Mr. Wong shared how the City of Glendale
  is doing in regarding the renewable portfolio and power content label. He provided a history
  and background regarding the RPS Program and explained the regulatory requirements and
  terminology. Mr. Wong described mitigation and compliance strategies (i.e., meeting
  compliance period soft targets, meeting IRP goals, and entering into long-term renewable
  and clean energy agreements) as well as the City’s Power Content Label. Mr. Wong stated
  that the City of Glendale had been the leader in achieving a higher renewable portfolio
  percentage than the neighboring utilities and the State of California. Finally, Messrs. Wong
  and Young responded to the Commissioners’ questions about EV cars, long-term plans for
  other projects (road map to 100% clean), and relative percentages of different types of
  renewables.

  b. 4kV to 12kV Conversion Program Update
  Daniel Scorza, Chief Assistant General Manager - Electric, presented the 4kV to 12kV
  Conversion Program Update. Mr. Scorza provided a background on why we need to do the
  conversions and the benefits of the conversions and described recent accomplishments and
  improvements by the Electric Services Section. He highlighted the conversion projects of the
  past five years (Tropico, Grandview, and Bel Aire Feeders) as well as ongoing conversion
  projects. In addition to the 12kV conversions, Mr. Scorza described GWP’s wildfire mitigation
  upgrade program, including installing covered overhead insulated wire and upgraded
  transformers that protect against problems with wildfires but prevents Mylar balloons and tree
  branches from being in contact with the distribution wire. Mr. Scorza responded to the
  Commissioners’ questions.

  c. Glendale Energy Center CEQA Update
  Due to time restraints (another City commission meeting was scheduled at 5:30pm), the
  Commissioners moved to continue this item to the March 1, 2021 Commission meeting.

6. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Victoria Valentine (resident) (regarding safe drinking water).

7. AGENDA FORECAST
  The Commissioners reviewed and approved the following agenda for the March 1, 2021 meeting:
   Reliability Report
   Governor’s Vehicle Electrification Goals- Impact on GWP
   Legislative Update
   Customer Services Update
   Water Conservation and Impact (per the request of Commissioner Jazmadarian, seconded
  with the concurrence of the other Commissioners)
   Glendale Energy Center CEQA Update
   Virtual Power Plant Update (per the request of President Flanigan)

8. ADJOURNMENT
  Motion to Adjourn:
  Moved by: Commissioner Kedikian
  Seconded by: Commissioner Lall
  Motion Passed.

The meeting was adjourned at 5:21 p.m.
